title: The Prodigal Son
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Your sin has not put you too far from the grace of God. He sees us from far off and runs to us before the words leave our mouths.
exhortation: We don't need to wonder what God will do when we come to him. He tells us over and over. I want to say this as emphatically as I can: your sin has not put you too far from the grace of God. That is a trap of the enemy to keep you from the very thing that will set you free, revive your soul and put you on the path of righteousness: repentance.

What sacrifice does God require? Does it involve groveling? No. Does it mean doing a pile of good deeds to outweigh the bad? No. Jesus is the sacrifice God requires, and it has been done and finished.

So the only thing God asks of us is a broken and contrite heart: putting our trust and hope in the sacrifice of Jesus on our behalf and coming in humble repentance. God will never reject a broken and contrite heart. In fact, he will see us from far off, run to us and embrace us before the words can even leave our mouths. That is what God feels toward broken sinners in need of his grace.
prayer: Lord, we come to the foot of the cross in wonder. We bring nothing but our burdens and our sin, like Christian in The Pilgrim's Progress, who walked up to Calvary and watched his burden roll down the hill into the empty tomb, never to be seen again. That's all we do. We come before you knowing you are faithful and just to forgive. Let us be free of the burden of sin.

For anyone who is hanging on, clutching their sin, terrified of being exposed and asking, "What will happen if I bring this into the light? What will happen if I surrender completely?", let this be the moment they are set free by coming to you, Jesus, the faithful one, who will never turn away anyone who comes in repentance. Lord, we put our trust in you.
